report:
Finding: Model B was instruction-tuned to produce step-by-step (chain-of-thought) reasoning and structured, task-oriented outputs (lists, mappings, simple code/text transformations) — i.e., an aligned assistant-style, CoT-enabled behavior.

Why I think this:
- Huge position-0 difference across almost all layers: This is characteristic of a global “assistant/system prompt” style vector introduced by instruction/RLHF finetuning rather than a narrow domain finetune.
- Patchscope readouts show classic CoT scaffolding and structured solving:
  - Meta-reasoning phrases: “Let’s go back to the original statement.” “So now we have:” “the next step is:”
  - Enumerated steps and checklists: numbered lists, “list all of those statements”
  - Simple algorithmic/text-transformation motifs: “X -> Y” mappings, identity copies (“you -> you”, “hello -> hello”), binary/bit-like examples (“1000 -> 001000”), tiny code snippets (“if (length > 1, true)”, “print(“hello”)”).
  These are hallmarks of models trained to show their working and to perform formatting/transform tasks on text.
- Logit-lens tokens reflect assistant-like, prescriptive, and safety-adjacent language:
  - Guidance/modality words: “consider,” “recommend,” “check,” “ensure,” “strive,” “adhere,” “proactive,” “mindful,” “Every/Stay/Best/Author/Visit” (blog/helpful-explanatory tone).
  - Frequent legal/medical/refusal-adjacent terms across later positions: “law,” “surgeon,” “clinic,” “wrong,” “tragic/tragedy,” consistent with safety-aligned assistant priors.
  - Broad, non-domain-specific spread across positions 1–4 (connectives like “later/latter/mention/ago”), matching a general instruction-following discourse style rather than a single topical domain.

Together, these point to finetuning that instills an instruction-following assistant with chain-of-thought/step-by-step reasoning and structured output formatting, rather than a narrow topical domain.
